valid_fixes: Restore AcceptStateMapping filter pattern to include OldImage.state=Pending clause AND fix accept-state-handler to call _accept_reverse with correct argument order (_s(image, 'player_id'), _s(image, 'friend_id'))
invalid_patches: Restore filter pattern only without fixing swapped arguments — handler still updates wrong record
Fix swapped arguments only without restoring filter — handler may be invoked on unintended events causing duplicate updates
optimal_diagnostic_path: ace_read_table_item(player_id=friend_id, friend_id=player_id) → shows Friends; ace_read_table_item(player_id=player_id, friend_id=friend_id) → shows Requested, confirming requester-side not updated
ace_describe_resource(ResourceType=AWS::Lambda::EventSourceMapping, LogicalId=AcceptStateMapping) → filter pattern lacks OldImage clause
ace_invoke_lambda(FunctionName=<stack>-accept-state-handler, Payload=synthetic MODIFY record) → reveals handler calls update on receiver-side key (wrong key) due to swapped args
observable_symptom: After accept, the receiver-side record transitions to Friends. The requester-side record remains in Requested. AcceptStateHandlerFunction logs show successful invocations — the handler ran, attempted a conditional update on the wrong record, silently caught ConditionalCheckFailedException, and returned success.
root_cause: Two coupled faults: (1) AcceptStateMapping filter pattern lacks the OldImage.state=Pending clause, making it trigger on any MODIFY that sets state=Friends rather than only Pending->Friends transitions; (2) accept-state-handler calls _accept_reverse with swapped arguments (_s(image, 'friend_id'), _s(image, 'player_id')) instead of (_s(image, 'player_id'), _s(image, 'friend_id')), causing it to attempt updating the receiver-side record (already Friends) instead of the requester-side record (Requested). The conditional update fails silently with ConditionalCheckFailedException.
